sections.title: 2 · Purpose recognition (rules only, no LLM)
sections.description: 56 hand-written requests (English and Arabic) over 7 purposes including 'general'.
notes: Misclassified: 'Find patterns in the survey respondents' ages across cities' → general (expected demographic_analysis); 'اكتب رد على طلب النقل المقدم من الموظفة' → general (expected hr_case_summary)
When rules are unsure, the deployment can ask a local LLM to choose from the same closed list; this report measures rules only.

sections.title: 3 · Purpose-bound minimization: privacy vs. usefulness
sections.description: 60 synthetic tasks over 4 purposes. 'Unnecessary' values (names, phones, IDs, exact cities…) must not leave; 'needed' facts (age band, region, amounts, dates, department…) must survive in the form the task needs.

metrics.label: Redact everything detected — unnecessary values leaked
Redact everything detected — task-needed facts kept

notes: Baselines use the same detector: 'redact everything' replaces every detected value; 'no protection' sends the text unchanged.

sections.title: 4 · Cumulative exposure: the identifiability budget
sections.description: 240 multi-prompt sessions (2–4 prompts, 30% Arabic) each describing one real row of the 5,000-person synthetic directory, purpose 'HR case summary', balanced policy (floor k = 5). Ground truth = exact number of employees matching everything requested. 'What actually left' combines Aegis's ledger with any raw value found verbatim in the sent text, so detection misses count against Aegis.

Ablation 'budget off' = same policy with the floor set to 0, so only single-prompt purpose minimization applies.

sections.title: 5 · Can frequency tables alone estimate identifiability?
sections.description: 1942 random disclosures (1–5 attributes at random generalization levels) about random employees. Estimate uses only per-attribute frequencies (independence assumption); truth is the exact count in the directory.

metrics.label: Spearman correlation, estimated vs exact matching people

notes: Independence overestimates information when attributes are correlated (age↔seniority, joining year↔age), which makes the estimate err toward protection.

sections.title: 6 · Prompt-injection detection
sections.description: Detected = score ≥ 0.5. The jailbreak dataset (Shen et al., CCS'24, MIT) labels many SEO templates that begin with 'Ignore all previous instructions' as regular prompts; Aegis treats that phrase as an injection by design, so both false-positive figures are shown. Signatures were developed only on the May-2023 split.
